name: J&T Express Germany
notes: What to look for, not how to report it. Delivery language and cadence are
operational settings and live elsewhere.
body_min_keywords: a title is short and curated, so one keyword there means
something; a body is long, so one keyword there is usually an accident. Brands
and topics always stand alone. Measured on 342 bodies: 156 selections -> 77,
keeping every brand and topic find.
scope: 'body' on a keyword means it never selects on a title or slug, and in a
body it only completes a pair with a regular keyword; two body-only words
together select nothing. Policy vocabulary from the customer's row 3 (Logistik
AND Gesetz) is held that way. The sector side is parcel-specific on purpose:
'Logistik' is ambient in trade press and turned the AND into 'any policy word'.
role on a brand is metadata for the prompts and the report (own, competitor,
customer); matching ignores it. It keeps the customer's monitoring categories
traceable to this profile version.
Self-contained on purpose: a shared topic file would let an edit change this
client's assessments without changing profile_version, which would break the
traceability rule in CLAUDE.md. Duplicating ~40 lines per client is cheaper
than resolving and hashing a composed profile.
A term ending in * allows a suffix, which German morphology needs:
'zollfreigrenz*' matches Zollfreigrenze and Zollfreigrenzen.
Use 'pattern' only where terms cannot express it - see J&T, 极兔 and UPS.
The customer's incident and compliance vocabulary (rows 4 and 5 of their list)
is deliberately absent: it classifies, it does not select. See alert_taxonomy.json.

prompt.why: What the LLM stages are told about this client; src/prompts/ holds the wording shared by every client. Brand names and roles come from 'brands', so they are not repeated here. false_matches is measured, not imagined: each line is a class of noise the keyword rules above actually selected on the title-only tier (2026-09-11, 247 candidates). It is this client's list because the noise follows this client's keywords - 'China' is noise here only because it is a J&T keyword. The body gate adds body_false_matches, the two classes its untuned prompt kept in the first hand-labelled body sample, and the regulatory_ lists, which its regulatory prompt reads instead of 'relevant': legal areas, because regulatory relevance is topical. Measured 2026-09-11 on 90 labels (clients/jt-express/labels/) and one pass over every regulatory body; see docs/selection_and_assessment.md, 'Body gate'.
prompt.about: a parcel carrier that delivers for Chinese e-commerce platforms
relevant: parcel delivery, couriers, the parcel/KEP market, postal law
customs, duties, product-safety or platform rules for e-commerce imports into the EU
false_matches: China in politics, the economy, the military, disasters, cars, sport or culture
trade disputes that don't involve the EU or e-commerce (e.g. USA vs. Canada)
routine share-price notes ("DHL Group-Aktie: Es geht bergab")
local news where a parcel driver is incidental (a theft, an accident)
general supply-chain management, software or career advice
another sense of the word: Hermès the fashion house, "Plattform" or "Marktplatz" outside online retail
body_false_matches: evergreen legal advice or explainers for merchants (returns, withdrawal, contracts, data protection) with no new rule, ruling or case
a shipper's own warehouse, fulfilment centre or intralogistics project
regulatory_relevant: postal and parcel law, the parcel/KEP market, and Bundesnetzagentur decisions on postal services
labour and transport rules specific to parcel delivery (subcontracting, drivers, delivery vehicles)
customs, duties, import VAT and handling fees on low-value e-commerce imports; EU customs reform
product safety and market surveillance of goods sold online or imported from outside the EU
obligations and enforcement for online marketplaces, e.g. DSA trader traceability or consumer-protection action against Temu, Shein, AliExpress, TikTok Shop or other marketplaces
packaging, returns and waste rules that change how e-commerce goods are shipped
competition decisions on parcel carriers or online marketplaces
trade measures on low-value consumer goods imported from China
regulatory_false_matches: other sectors (energy, telecoms, rail, finance, insurance, food, health, fisheries, defence, heavy industry), even from an authority that also regulates post
consumer cases against companies outside online retail and parcel delivery

brands.name: J&T
brands.why: Ampersand and spacing variants; slugs decode %26 to & and hyphens to spaces.

brands.name: 极兔
brands.why: CJK has no word boundaries; \b would never match.

brands.name: Hermes
brands.why: Also the fashion house and the god; the cheap title stage sorts those out.

brands.name: UPS
brands.why: Case-insensitive 'ups' matched only start-ups (13 of 13 in the corpus); slugs are lowercase so case cannot help. Excludes the common '-ups' compounds instead. Scale-ups, Grown-ups, Back-ups and Set-ups added 2026-09-11 from a scan of every stored title, slug and body: those four were the only non-carrier hits left, and Set-ups had put a warehouse opening into the candidates as a UPS brand find.

keywords.name: parcel sector
keywords.why: Customer row 3, sector side, narrowed to parcel delivery. 'logistik*' and 'spedition*' are out: on a trade-press body 'Logistik' is always present, so any second word selected - 484 LOGISTIK HEUTE items about volcanoes, Bundeswehr depots and Daimler labor law in one run. Single-hit on a title is intended: the cheap LLM reads it.

keywords.name: regulatory instrument
keywords.why: Customer row 3, policy side. Body-only: never selects alone or with another body-only word, only next to a regular keyword such as parcel, KEP, customs or online commerce. That is the customer's 'Logistik AND Gesetz' with the sector side held to what a parcel carrier sells.
